privacy_purpose: To share launch news and the first invitation

privacy_optional: Survey answers such as your role and current AI tasks are optional, and are used only to set the order of first invitations.
survey_intro: Want an earlier invite? 30 seconds more — what you tell us sets the order.
survey_job_label: What kind of work do you do?
survey_ai_label: What do you mostly use AI for these days?
survey_job_other_label: Other — what kind of work do you do?

survey_done: Thank you. We'll keep this in mind.

confirm_email_sent: We sent a welcome email — take a look in your inbox.

confirm_next: From here, we'll send you notes from the build now and then.
confirm_world_tagline: Another me, in the digital world
confirm_mos_line: I've remembered your name. You'll be the first one I call.

meta_title: mosmos — a world where my AI grows up
meta_description: Just say it. Mos does the moving. A personal AI for people who research, organise and write things up. We invite the front row first.
hero_tagline: A world where my AI grows up
hero_sub: Just say it. Mos does the moving.
hero_gloss: Mos — the AI that settles the goal with you and brings the result back
hero_anchor: A personal AI for people who research, organise and write things up
mos_poke_2: That tickles. Shall we get started?
mos_poke_4: Leave your name and I'll remember it.
ache: If getting AI to do the work became work of its own
decide_lead: Then I hand it to the right specialist and bring the result back. Pick one.
decide_g1: Tell me only what changed in competitors' pricing this week
decide_g2: Pull just the decisions out of yesterday's minutes
decide_g3: Point out the risky clauses in this contract
decide_ask2: Should I match owners to them?
decide_hand: I'll hand this to the right specialist.
decide_r1: Two of six pricing pages changed. Only the changed rows are in the table.
decide_r2: Four decisions pulled out. One on hold, carried to the next meeting.
decide_r3: Three high-risk clauses flagged, each with wording to use instead.
decide_cost: The run finished, so it came off for what was used
decide_note: Light work Mos does on the spot; heavier work goes to a Mon. Either way it comes off after the work finishes, and only for what was used.
watch_title: Say it once and it keeps watching
watch_lead: Write what to watch for as a sentence. If there is nothing worth saying, it stays quiet.
watch_memo_hint: Shorter is better · Checking on its own costs no Mana
watch_memo_1: Tell me when Mana is running low
watch_memo_2: Tell me if something urgent lands in my inbox
watch_memo_3: Summarise new comments on the shared docs
watch_memo_4: Give me a short note if a competitor page changes
watch_add: Write one line to watch for
watch_beat_state: Checks every 30 minutes · nothing to report right now
watch_cron_lead: Anything you want pinned to a time gets booked here
watch_note: It runs at the time you set. For anything you cannot pin to a time, leave it to watching.
make_lead: No code. Write down the job, connect the tools it needs. Try tapping below.
make_io_note: A Mon talks to Mos, not to a person. So it is the same for every Mon, and there is nothing to choose.
make_brain_hint: You do not need to know model names. Pick what it mostly does and a fitting one is attached.
make_tier_1_d: Handles short sorting and tidying very quickly.
make_tier_2_d: Balances speed and accuracy across most document work.
make_tier_3_d: Pushes hard judgement calls and their reasoning all the way through.
make_prompt_hint: One empty box is hard to fill. It comes in three pieces.
make_pp_role_h: What kind of Mon this is, in a sentence or two
make_pp_role_b: A Mon that reads contracts and terms, and finds the clauses that could be risky. It looks first at the ones people tend to miss.
make_pp_steps_h: The order it works in · number the lines and it follows them
make_pp_steps_b:
1. Find the termination, auto-renewal, liability and confidentiality clauses first.
2. Mark any sentence judged risky, with where it sits in the original.
3. Give the reason in one line.
4. Suggest wording to use instead.
make_pp_keep_h: What it must do, and what it must not
make_pp_keep_b:
Never state this as legal advice.
Quote clauses as written; do not rewrite them.
When something needs checking, ask instead of guessing.
make_pp_all_h: The three pieces joined up. Not edited here.
make_palette_hint: Tap to attach, tap again to take it off
make_c_notion_d: Reads pages and writes new ones
make_c_github_d: Reads and writes repos and issues
make_c_ppx_d: Finds it and sorts the sources too
make_c_exa_d: Give it an address, it brings back the text
make_c_browser_d: Uses the web in a window of its own
make_c_s1_d: A Skill bought on the Hub
make_note: Making costs no Mana. It is open on every plan.
share_title: Put the Mon you made on the Hub
share_lead: When someone else's Mos picks your Mon, part of what they spend comes back to you.
share_free_d: Whoever runs it pays only what the run costs. Nothing comes back to you.
share_paid_d: Every time it runs, part of what comes off goes to you.
share_skill_d: You are paid once, when it is bought. Runs after that cost the buyer nothing extra.
share_listed: How it looks on the Hub
share_mine_desc: Flags risk per clause and suggests wording to use instead.
share_peer_1_m: Gathers material and sums it up weekly
share_peer_2_m: Pulls just the decisions out of meeting notes
share_review_label: Two kinds of feedback get left
share_review_mos: What Mos records — the Mos that gave it work note whether it saw the job through
share_review_patron: What people write — from someone who used it
share_note: There is no plan limit on making or publishing. The Hub and payouts are still being built, so we will say when they open.
cost_lead: One is the monthly subscription. The other is Mana, which only drops when work actually runs. Neither one replaces the other.
cost_sub: Subscription — what you pay each month
cost_sub_d: It covers what stays switched on: your account, your storage, runs at a set time.
cost_p1_role: Come in and see one task through from start to finish.
cost_p2_role: For everyday use. Runs at a set time open up here.
cost_p3_role: For heavy use. Your work goes first when things pile up.
cost_d_logs: How long run records are kept
cost_d_queue: Order of work when things pile up
cost_open: The same on every plan — making Mons, keeping them, putting them on the Hub
cost_amounts_tbd: How much storage, and how long records are kept, are still being worked out.
cost_mana: Mana — the balance that only drops when work runs
cost_mana_d: It pays for calling the AI model and using tools. It comes off after the work finishes, and only for what was used.
cost_no: This is when it does not
cost_a1: Asking Mos for something and getting the result
cost_a1_d: It comes off once, after the work finishes. Nothing is taken up front.
cost_a2: Running a Mon you borrowed from the Hub
cost_a2_d: Part of what comes off goes to the person who made that Mon.
cost_a3: Buying a Skill on the Hub
cost_a3_d: It comes off once, when you buy it. Running it later costs nothing more.
cost_b2: Keeping a Mon you made in storage
cost_b3: Looking through other people's Mons on the Hub
cost_mana_tbd: How much a single run takes, and what Mana itself costs, are still being worked out.
cost_note: We have not set prices yet. We would rather ask the people who use it first, then decide. Once it is settled, everyone who leaves their name here hears first.
join_title: As soon as it's ready, the front row hears first
join_scarcity: The pilot goes out to a small, selected group.
trust_care: Your email is used only for launch and pilot news, and notes from the build.
world_island_label: The sky island Mos lives on
